requirements.title: List-directed null values are r*, empty fields, or leading empty first fields
requirements.definition: A null value is specified by r*, by no characters between consecutive value separators, or by no characters before the first value separator in the first record read for the input statement.

requirements.title: List-directed null values preserve definition status and cannot be complex parts
requirements.definition: A null value has no effect on the next effective item definition status; it shall not be used for either complex part, but one null may represent an entire complex constant.

pending.single-null-entire-complex: Initialize complex z=(1.0,2.0); internal READ record ',' into z followed by another item; expected z remains approximately (1.0,2.0).
pending.null-not-complex-part: Deferred input-error plan: '(,2.0)' differs from '(1.0,2.0)' only by a null real part; observe IOSTAT if Clause 12 makes it portable, not a diagnostic.

requirements.title: Slash terminates list-directed input and null-supplies remaining effective items
requirements.definition: A slash value separator terminates the input statement after the previous value, ignores the rest of the record, and supplies null values for additional effective items and input-list do-variables as needed.

pending.slash-ignores-rest: Same record '1 / not_an_integer' into x,y; expected no attempt to parse trailing text after slash when portable IOSTAT context is supplied.

S13.10.3.2-003 slash termination runtime fixtures: two complete run/effect programs initialize nonzero sentinels before slash input. Record '1 / 99' assigns x=1 and leaves y=-802, proving termination after the previous value and null-supply for the remaining item. Record '1 /' read into [501,602,703] yields [1,602,703], proving additional effective items are left unchanged. Deleting the slash makes the trailing value visible or causes a count failure.
